topic: Meta delays AI scraping terms after publisher backlash
headline_marked: [[Meta delays new business terms]] after publisher pushback on AI scraping
headline: Meta delays new business terms after publisher pushback on AI scraping
summary: Meta has pushed back the enforcement of its new business terms to November 20th, following concerns from publishers that the terms could allow the company to scrape news sites for AI training.
details: Meta has postponed the enforcement of its new business terms until November 20th. This decision comes after significant backlash from publishers globally who raised concerns about potential AI scraping. The terms were originally set to take effect on October 30th.

The controversial terms appeared to grant Meta permission to freely scrape news sites that utilize its platforms. Publishers feared this material would then be used for training Meta's AI models, despite Meta updating the language to remove explicit mention of "training."

Legal experts argued that the revised wording was still insufficient to prevent the possibility of AI data scraping. Organizations like the News/Media Alliance sent a letter to Mark Zuckerberg, demanding revisions to prevent "severe harm" to publishers.

Digital advertisers and publishers in the European Union and the UK also pressured regulators to intervene and halt the new terms. Meta spokesperson Daniel Roberts stated the delay allows more time to explain the changes to partners and stakeholders.

Roberts also clarified that content owners will still be able to use robots.txt to signal their preferences regarding web crawlers. This file is a standard method for websites to communicate with bots about which parts of their site should or should not be crawled.

topic: Amazon scraps AI data center plans due to local backlash
headline_marked: [[Amazon scraps plans to build four new data centers]] in Northern Virginia after local backlash
headline: Amazon scraps plans to build four new data centers in Northern Virginia after local backlash
summary: The company will instead repurpose the 122-acre site for mixed-use and residential development, donating 25 acres for a community arts center and recreational facility, plus $5 million for housing.
details: Amazon will no longer build four new data centers on the George Washington University's campus in Loudoun County, Virginia. This decision follows significant pushback from the local community regarding concerns about noise and power consumption.

Instead, Amazon will repurpose the majority of the 122-acre site for mixed-use and residential development. The company will also donate 25 acres to Loudoun County for a community arts center and recreational facility, and contribute $5 million to the county's housing fund.

Loudoun County is known as "Data Center Alley" due to its high concentration of data centers. However, residents' concerns about noise and the immense power requirements of these facilities have led to a shift in the county's approach to new data center construction.

Josh Weissman, Amazon’s VP of data center development, stated that while the company saw the property's legal development potential differently, they opted for a shared vision with the county. This decision was made to avoid costly litigation and foster a collaborative outcome.

The recent boom in AI use has dramatically increased demand for additional and larger data centers. This growing demand is often met with opposition from local communities concerned about impacts like electricity price spikes, water shortages, and deforestation.
